acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: A task PR that lowers its own risk_level is blocked and still requires a Guardian.
A task PR that widens its own locks, or edits any other governance field of its own contract, is blocked.
A first-registration PR whose task file is absent at base still passes.
The full suite, the governance-evidence and adversarial suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: The Guardian requirement is derived from the HEAD task's risk_level (`_guardian_risk_labels` feeding `_builtin_guardian_risk_required`). Measured directly: head risk_level critical -> guardian_required True; head risk_level low -> guardian_required False.

Nothing compares a normal task PR's own task file to the base snapshot. `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` blocks deleting a task file and blocks touching a FOREIGN task file, but leaves the PR's own task file unconstrained; `tasks` is not in `_GENERIC_MIRROR_DIRS`; and `_frozen_task_match_errors` is reached only from `_enforce_frozen_registration` (contract and goal_reconcile modes). Driving the gate directly with base risk_level=critical and head risk_level=low produced ZERO blocking reasons and guardian_required=False.

ADR 0015 already decided this and stated the resolution rule: 'the base snapshot is authority when the contract exists in it; otherwise head is authority; and risk may never resolve weaker than base.' The base-when-present half matters — the goal loop registers a task's contract on the task branch, so at the merge base the contract does not exist for a first-registration PR, and a base-only rule would block every implementation PR while simultaneously disengaging the gate.

Every gate this repository added on 2026-07-29/31 — contract approval, the bookkeeping-closeout exemption, the reduced approval count — sits on top of this hole. A PR that can lower its own risk can opt out of all of it.

Scope was checked against locks before freezing: every file any scope item touches (scripts/mergegate_check.py, tests/test_contract_immutability.py, scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh, scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh) is inside the declared locks, and all four are currently unheld. This check was skipped when writing T-…48021407 and cost that task two Spec Amendments.
grill_with_docs.source: Measured 2026-07-31 while verifying the ADR 0017 rollout.

non_goals: Blocking the lifecycle fields a task PR legitimately writes: status, expected_pr, closeout_pr, expected_branch, ledger_evidence.
Changing contract, goal_reconcile, post_merge_reconcile or bookkeeping-closeout handling — each already has its own immutability rule and must keep it.
Requiring a base snapshot: a first-registration PR adds its own task file and must still pass.
Changing how risk_level is resolved for the Guardian gate beyond refusing a weaker-than-base value.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: An implementation PR can no longer lower its own risk_level to disengage its own Guardian gate, widen its own locks to escape lock scope, or edit any other governance field of its own task contract. ADR 0015 decided this; it was implemented for contract, goal_reconcile and post_merge_reconcile PRs and never for the normal task-PR path, which is the path almost every PR takes.
title: Stop a task PR from rewriting the contract that governs it
